blocks.content: We had another busy and fun-filled week at Kramer! Our 4th graders had a great time on Monday visiting Miami Softball Team. We are so thankful for the time they spent with our students and for all they do to keep our community safe! We hope everyone has a wonderful weekend, and we look forward to another great week at Kramer!

title: Grading System Changes and District Policies
source_title: Kramer Elementary | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
Important 

District 

Information Important District Information

Changes to the K-5 Grading System at Talawanda  NEW for the 2026-2027 School Year Grades 3-5 - Moving to a Traditional Letter Grading System (A-F)We are excited to shift our grades 3–5 to a traditional letter grade system (A-F) to provide a more detailed look at your child's overall performance and academic habits. This change aligns our 3rd-5th graders with the expectations they will meet in middle and high school, fostering greater accountability and preparing them for future success.For families, this transition offers a familiar and intuitive way to track progress. While the numerical scale focused on specific milestones, letter grades allow for a wider range of feedback to distinguish between meeting basic requirements and consistently exceeding them. This system ensures a clearer dialogue between teachers and parents, highlighting exactly where a student excels or may need extra support.Here is the breakdown of the traditional letter grading system:A - 90-100%B - 80-89%C - 70-79%D - 60-69%F - 0-59%Grades K-2 - Remaining with the Numerical Grading System (1-4)Grades K–2 will continue using the numerical (1–4) grading system to best support our youngest learners. At this foundational level, education is focused on the progressive development of core skills and meeting specific developmental milestones rather than a cumulative letter grade. The 1–4 scale provides a precise way for teachers to communicate exactly where a student is in their learning journey—from beginning to explore a concept to achieving mastery—ensuring that families have a clear understanding of their child's growth in these critical early years. As a reminder, here is a breakdown of the numerical scores:4 - Consistently/Independently Meeting the Standard3 - Meeting the Standard2 - Approaching the Standard1- Not Yet Meeting the Standard

TSD Title I-A Parent and Family Engagement Policy We invite and encourage our families to review the TSD Title I-A Parent and Family Engagement Policy linked to our website. If you have feedback to share, please contact your student’s Title Reading teacher. There will also be a feedback session on 11/19/26 ahead of the School Board Meeting at the THS Performing Art Center.

TSD One Plan Family Engagement We invite and encourage our families to review the TSD One Plan linked to our website. Talawanda is in year one of our current One Plan. Additional information about the One Plan can be found on the Ohio Department of Education and Workforce, linked here.If you have feedback to share or would like to be part of the parent/community advisory group for our One Plan, please contact Ms. Stephanie Aerni, Director of Teaching & Learning (AerniS@talawanda.org). There will also be a feedback session on 11/19/26 ahead of the School Board Meeting at the THS Performing Art Center.

summary: **Major grading changes for 2026-2027:** Grades 3-5 are moving to a traditional letter grading system (A-F with A=90-100%, B=80-89%, C=70-79%, D=60-69%, F=0-59%), while grades K-2 will continue using the numerical 1-4 system. Families are invited to review the **TSD Title I-A Parent and Family Engagement Policy** and the **TSD One Plan** on the district website. A **feedback session for both policies** will be held on **11/19/26** ahead of the School Board Meeting at the THS Performing Art Center. To join the parent/community advisory group or provide feedback, contact Ms. Stephanie Aerni (AerniS@talawanda.org) or your student's Title Reading teacher.

title: RAH Reading at Home Program Launch
source_title: Kramer Elementary | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content: RAH RAH

Attention Kindergarten, 1st, and 2nd grade families: RAH begins on Wednesday September 30th. This will be our first redemption day, so please return your RAH sheet by Wednesday!Kramer RAH (Reading At Home) is a voluntary program from K-2nd graders that builds a home-school connection by rewarding students for reading at home. Each week students record the books they've read and turn-in record sheets for rewards. Rewards alternate between a student selected book and a small prize.

Family support and involvement are important! Here’s how it works:Read a book, color a book. Books can be read to, by, or with your child. Books can be read multiple times and you can color a book for each time a book is read. Ten pages of a chapter book counts as one book. Fill the page with 20 books read.Send the completed sheet to school with your child on WEDNESDAYS. The first sheet is on the back of this flyer, but any paper with your child’s name and teacher’s name is fine; just draw a star (or other symbol/shape) to represent each book read. Your child will receive a prize for each sheet with 20 books completed!Students will only receive 1 prize a week. However, you may send in up to 2 completed sheets if your child reads beyond 20 books in a week. We will hold on to the extra sheet, using it if your child has missed a Wednesday or forgotten their sheet. Any remaining extra sheets will be tallied at the end of the year. Classrooms that read 1,000 books every 6 weeks will receive a class reward!

summary: The **RAH (Reading At Home) program** for grades K-2 begins **Wednesday, September 30th**, which is the first redemption day. Students record books read at home (books read to, by, or with child; 10 pages of chapter book = 1 book) and submit sheets with 20 books on **Wednesdays** for rewards alternating between books and prizes. Families can submit up to 2 completed sheets per week, and classrooms reading 1,000 books every 6 weeks receive a class reward.
